slides.title: Fragmented records make accountability difficult
slides.subtitle: Workforce, harvest and payments often live in separate records
bullets: Reconciling employee hours with harvested quantities
Connecting inventory, actual consumption and costs
Separating agreed rates, earned amounts and real payments
Finding buyers and available workers
slides.notes: Describe problems observed in practice. Do not claim all farms use paper or that competing systems do not exist. Loss amounts and market-wide prevalence have not been measured. About 50 seconds.

slides.title: Built from day-to-day plantation experience
slides.subtitle: Domain knowledge and development alongside users
bullets: Needs identified through six years of agricultural experience
Development shaped by real users and their requirements
Focus: clear records, harvest control and employee trust
slides.notes: The founder supplied the six-year experience statement. Answer public questions using only facts approved for sharing. About 45 seconds.

slides.title: Connect the steps of one working process
slides.subtitle: Plan → Execute → Harvest → Inventory → Results
bullets: Records link to the company, employee and source activity
Planning, actual execution and payment are separate events
Goal: decisions that can be checked against source records
slides.notes: This diagram represents the business workflow. It does not certify universal automatic posting between every module. Inspect the resulting inventory and financial records. About 50 seconds.

slides.title: Harvest records you can trace
slides.subtitle: Worker, crate, weight, sector and agreed rate
bullets: Configure a session for the actual harvesting method
Identify worker and crate; verify gross, tare and net
Review individual records before payroll
Test scanner and scale compatibility on the intended device
slides.notes: Show the actual operational interface. Do not promise universal scanner, scale or NFC compatibility. Passive NFC cards do not supply GPS themselves. The separate terminal pilot stages records only. About 55 seconds.

slides.title: Workers can see what they earned
slides.subtitle: A shared source of work and payment history
bullets: Picked quantities and recorded hours
Accrued, paid and outstanding amounts shown separately
CV, services, availability and reviews
Personal records limited to the authorized user

slides.title: Built for more than one crop
slides.subtitle: Initial sales focus on selected commercial farms
bullets: Vineyards, hazelnuts, citrus, orchards, blueberries and other crops
Proposed paying segment: plantations above 3 hectares
The free tier connects workers, specialists and companies
Size the addressable market by crop, area and willingness to pay
slides.notes: Total agricultural holdings are not the paying market. Supplied market figures have not been checked against primary sources. A 1–5 hectare band cannot identify the exact number above 3 hectares. No unverified TAM or revenue forecast is printed. About 50 seconds.

slides.title: Find companies, workers and offers
slides.subtitle: Regional discovery and communication in one platform
bullets: Search companies, crops and job announcements
Offer services and agree terms directly
Make batch information clearer during the sales process

slides.title: Farmers decide what to share—and with whom
slides.subtitle: Preview and edit before sharing: a planned feature concept
bullets: Three modes: live harvest, completed batch or manually prepared offer
Public visibility or selected companies and users
Control each camera’s access separately
Changing offered quantity does not overwrite harvest records
slides.notes: This is an interactive UI concept, not a production integration. Server authorization, verified identities and video-gateway access are required. A completion timestamp alone is not independent proof of freshness. About 60 seconds.

slides.title: The value is in connected workflows
slides.subtitle: Combine farm operations with a useful partner network
bullets: Connected work history instead of isolated records
An employee view alongside the management workspace
Partner and job discovery alongside farm management
Validate differentiation and benefits through real pilots
slides.notes: This is positioning, not an independently verified competitor comparison. Georgian and international farm-management systems exist. Avoid unique/only claims and unsupported competitor limitations. Eye2Eye informed the narrative structure, not AgriMap facts. About 45 seconds.

slides.title: Free entry; paid commercial use
slides.subtitle: Proposed prices to validate with customers
bullets: Core platform free for plantations up to 3 hectares
Above 3 hectares: GEL 150 per month per farm workspace
AI packages: GEL 10–150; AI included in the GEL 150 subscription
Pricing and AI usage conditions still need validation
slides.notes: These are proposed prices, not achieved revenue or evidence of deployed billing. Unlimited AI needs separate cost and fair-use analysis. Local knowledge retrieval is not the same as proven model training. About 55 seconds.
slides.callout: GEL 150 / month = GEL 1,800 / year per farm

slides.title: From interest to active use
slides.subtitle: Start onboarding before peak season with a small, testable workflow
bullets: Targeted social campaigns and product demonstrations
Sales team follows up inquiries and prepares offers
Initial setup, training and a first complete session
Support and development driven by user feedback
slides.notes: Do not fix the number of new staff. The rollout accounts for seasonal workload and time needed for training. About 50 seconds.

slides.title: From working software to measurable growth
slides.subtitle: Software and screens exist; commercial outcomes need pilot evidence
bullets: Modules for harvest, workforce, inventory, finance, agronomy and communication
Documented workflows, illustrated help and access tests
Planned AI assistant to analyze user problems and feature requests
Automated testing and auditing developed with human oversight
slides.notes: Screens and tests do not establish complete commercial readiness or universal integration support. Measure onboarding time, active use, corrections and willingness to pay. Do not claim unmeasured 10× speed or 100% improvement from bots. About 50 seconds.

slides.title: GEL 25,000 to strengthen market entry
slides.subtitle: Program grant purpose: marketing, sales and farmer onboarding
bullets: Strengthen sales and farmer-onboarding capabilities
Targeted marketing and demonstration materials
Move interested farms from demos into active use
Accelerator support with sales channels and marketing
slides.notes: The program grant has not been presented as awarded funding. Do not invent spending splits or headcount. Prepare the detailed budget from real costs and program eligibility. This ends the core pitch; the next three slides support questions. About 55 seconds.

slides.title: What information connects the modules?
slides.subtitle: Keep each relationship tied to its source and company
bullets: Map data supplies sector, crop and variety to work and harvest
Worker identity links operational records to personal history
Harvest finalization determines inventory or sales handling
Accruals, payments and material movements remain separate checks
slides.notes: organizationId is the workspace boundary; employeeId/userId identifies the person; harvestEventId links weighings to a session. Replacing a stale whole array is not a universal safe merge. The separate terminal does not post operational payroll or stock. Appendix; outside the core timing.

slides.title: Share a controlled projection
slides.subtitle: A public offer must not expose internal company data
bullets: Keep the source harvest and marketplace offer separate
Server verifies the owner, company and recipient identity
Camera access requires permission to both the batch and that camera
Plan revocation, expiry, audit records and short-lived video access
slides.notes: This is planned architecture, not an implemented production whitelist in current Firestore rules. Display IDs must map to verified identities. Do not place authentication tokens or RTSP passwords in URLs or public documents. Client-side hiding is not access control. A timestamp is not a quality certificate. Appendix.

slides.title: Cloud, LAN and offline—with clear limits
slides.subtitle: Distinguish operational workflows from planned integrations
bullets: Cloud and local accounts are independent identities
Cloud backup is manual; universal automatic two-way merging is incomplete
Weather, cameras and sensors require gateways and tested integrations
AI recommendations require agronomist review
slides.notes: Do not present planned expansion as a completed autonomous system. LoRaWAN carries small sensor messages, not video. Live AI needs a configured server and authorization. Local knowledge lookup is not model training. The mentor video exceeded the transfer limit and the shared-chat text was unavailable; neither was analyzed. Appendix.
